page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, providing a 1.0 thread-per-core topology. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core and memory performance alongside weaker single-core execution. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and Passmark CPU score both place in the average tier, while single-core stress-ng and single-threaded gzip compression benchmarks fall into the lower 25th percentile. Memory bandwidth is solid, with cached small-block reads reaching 389.93 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 49.43 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance are average, with Redis handling 6.84 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r6.2xlarge provides a dense memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which aligns with its 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth. This instance is best suited for memory-intensive applications such as caching layers, relational databases, in-memory data structures, and general-purpose enterprise workloads requiring a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio.
